title: Why the line with one full cart is faster
description:
Every shopper at a checkout costs two kinds of time: about 3 seconds per item scanned, and about 48 seconds per person for the hello, paying, bagging and receipt. So one shopper with 50 items takes about 3 min 18 s, while four shoppers with 10 items each take about 5 min 12 s. Each person ahead of you is worth about 16 items, and a single cart beats four 10-item baskets until it holds 88 items.

Numbers checked in code (verify.py), including a 100,000-trial simulation with random shoppers (the cart finished first 99.5% of the time). Timings: Dan Meyer's 2009 checkout measurements (48 s per person, 2.8-2.9 s per item), rounded to 3 s.

facts_checked: Dan Meyer's 2009 checkout timing: 'Each item adds 2.9 seconds on average, but each person adds 48 seconds on average' (https://scienceblogs.com/principles/2009/09/13/grocery-store-science, fetched 2026-11-28); 2.8 s per item in other reports (https://chowhound.com/1579313/mistake-grocery-shopping-express-checkout-lane); later figures 41 s and ~3 s (https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/how-to-spend-less-time-in-grocery-store-lines-163041654.html). The video rounds to 48 s and 3 s.

Cart 48 + 50 x 3 = 198 s (3:18); baskets 4 x 48 + 40 x 3 = 312 s (5:12); difference 114 s; 48 / 3 = 16; 16 + 50 = 66, 4 x 16 + 40 = 104; cart faster up to 87 items, tie at 88 (verify.py). With 48/2.9, 48/2.8 and 41/3 the cart still wins (193 vs 308, 188 vs 304, 191 vs 284).
Simulation, 100,000 trials with random per-person (sd 20 s) and per-item (sd 1.5 s) times: cart first 99.5%, means 198 s and 312 s (verify.py)

beats.say: Four small baskets, or one full cart? One line is 2 minutes faster.
You'd count the items. 40 beats 50. But that's the wrong thing to count.
A math teacher timed real checkouts with a stopwatch. Every shopper runs two clocks.
Clock one: each item takes about 3 seconds to scan.
Clock two: every person takes 48 seconds. Hello, pay, bag, receipt, goodbye. Even with one item.
So time the cart. 50 items is 150 seconds, plus one person, 48. That's 3 minutes 18.
